experiment_name: NCM-A1: ANSWER-level parallel generation - batched pool of K whole answers with genius-weight logit mixing, then genius reasons over the pool and refines to one answer
user_theory_under_test: Mix genius weights with the normal model weights so both hold the context together; instead of generating one token (or one short block), generate MULTIPLE WHOLE ANSWERS together; the genius then reasons over those answers and refines them into ONE answer. Speed should come from generating many tokens at once; accuracy should come from reasoning over the pool.
why_answer_level_can_win_on_speed_where_: C1/BR-1 token-level blocks capped at ~1.01x because each proposed block costs an extra verify forward and blocks average ~1 extra token. On this CPU, decode is memory-bandwidth-bound (~988 MB weights read per forward): batching K=4 whole-answer rollouts into one forward produces 4 tokens per weight-read, amortizing the dominant cost - a real mechanism, not a marginal one.
parent: br1 (heads d2885e6b..., digit-dense prompt, eval set 7+43k) - genius heads are ALREADY compiled and RAM-resident; no new compile, no new training

model_frozen.note: GATE-3 re-verified at run start; same heads as BR-1 (RAM-resident genius weights 'waiting for weights to come' - they are already here)

pool_protocol_frozen.mixing_rule: per decode step, for rollout rows with alpha>0: logits[u] += alpha * z_u for u in U (12 frozen universe ids), where z_u = H1 genius head standardized score for class u at the current hidden state (the genius is literally mixed into the model's output weights at generation time; both hold the context together)
pool_protocol_frozen.decoding: greedy per rollout (deterministic, no sampling, no RNG); K rollouts batched in ONE forward per step (left-padded prompts, per-row EOS handling: finished rows keep emitting EOS, excluded from token counts)
pool_protocol_frozen.prompt: same digit-dense prompt as BR-1 (fewshot train items 0,1 digit-dense, same instruction string)
pool_protocol_frozen.items: GSM8K test indices [7+43*k for k in 0..29] (same frozen 30 as C1/BR-1)
pool_protocol_frozen.per_step_capture: chosen-token full-vocab logprob, H1 max z (confidence), H1 argmax agreement flag for tokens in U, per-row generated ids

selection_protocol_frozen.candidate_answer: decoded rollout text; strict value = '#### N' if present else last number (abstention counts wrong - consistent with all prior arms)
selection_protocol_frozen.genius_score_frozen: mean over answer-region generated tokens t of (agreement_t * conf_t) where agreement_t = 1 if H1 argmax == generated token and generated token in U else 0, conf_t = H1 max z; candidates with zero U tokens score -inf (ranked last)
selection_protocol_frozen.logprob_score_frozen: mean full-vocab logprob of generated tokens (length-normalized)
selection_protocol_frozen.fusion_score_frozen: z-score(genius_score) + z-score(logprob_score) across the K candidates of the same item (z over K=4 values; if a score is constant across candidates, its z contribution is 0)

selection_arms.sel_genius: argmax genius_score - the genius reasons over the pool and picks one answer
selection_arms.sel_logprob: argmax logprob_score - the model alone picks one answer (no-genius control)

selection_protocol_frozen.oracle_diagnostic: any candidate strict-correct in pool (pool ceiling; separate generation failure from selection failure, same philosophy as the KGAT oracle)

gates_frozen.GATE-H_heads_identity: wspl_br1_heads.npz sha256 == d2885e6b... at run start
gates_frozen.GATE-alpha0_anchor: alpha=0 rollout must reproduce BR-1 arm-A answers on >= 28/30 items (same prompt, same greedy; small fp differences from batched forwards allowed) - anchors pool validity

verdict_bands_frozen.accuracy: best selection arm strict vs A_br 36.67%: SUCCESS >= 46.67% (+10pp); PARTIAL >= 41.67% (+5pp); FAIL otherwise; reference line: C1 verbose baseline 50.0%
verdict_bands_frozen.speed: aggregate tok/s of the batched pool (all K rollout tokens / wall) vs A_br 8.69: SUCCESS >= 1.5x; PARTIAL >= 1.2x; FAIL otherwise
verdict_bands_frozen.genius_signal: sel_genius >= sel_logprob strict -> genius adds selection signal: YES / NO
verdict_bands_frozen.diversity_diagnostic: share of items whose pool contains >= 2 distinct final answers (target >= 0.5, else mixing failed to diversify - disclosed, no band)

hypotheses.H-A1-speed: batched whole-answer generation reaches >= 1.2x aggregate tok/s (memory-bandwidth amortization)
hypotheses.H-A1-diversity: genius-logit mixing creates pool diversity (>= 2 distinct answers in >= 50% of items)
hypotheses.H-A1-acc: genius reasoning over the pool refines to an answer at least +5pp above the single-greedy baseline without dropping below it
hypotheses.H-A1-genius: the genius selection signal beats pure model logprob selection

amendments: amendment_1 (disclosed, PRE-RESULTS, first 7-item slice VOIDED): raw-z mixing measured ineffective - diagnostic on item 7 (60 decode steps): median margin top-logit minus best-digit-logit = 14.81 (p10 1.66, p90 17.55) vs median z_max = 0.29 (p90 0.44); flip rates with raw z: alpha 0.5->0.0%, 1->0.0%, 2->1.67%, 4->1.67%, 8->3.33%; all four alpha rows produced identical answers on every voided item. New frozen rule: per step per row, z_hat = z / max|z| (max-normalized, sign preserved; zero if max|z|=0), mixed logits lg[U] += alpha * z_hat with alpha grid {0, 4, 8, 16} - alpha=4 flips only the lowest-margin steps, alpha=8 the lower quartile zone, alpha=16 flips ~half the steps (margin p50 14.8 < 16). Rationale: spans model-led to genius-led mixing; genius confidence magnitude is intentionally discarded by max-normalization (disclosed limitation). No results were reported from the voided slice.

amendment_2 (disclosed, PRE-RESULTS, 4-item interim slice VOIDED): max-normalized mixing works mechanically (alpha=4 changes answers) but alpha=8/16 degenerate to digit soup - genius digit bias injected mid-calculation corrupts arithmetic (observed preds 2e+306, inf on items 7/50/93/136; alpha=0 anchor still matches A_br exactly). New frozen pool row spec: row0 = greedy anchor (alpha=0, no mixing), row1 = genius-mixed greedy alpha=4 (z_hat rule unchanged), row2 = pure-model sampling T=0.8, row3 = pure-model sampling T=1.0; sampling seeds frozen: torch.Generator(seed=1000003*item_idx + row_index) per rollout, multinomial on softmax(logits/T); sampling rows have NO genius mixing (clean attribution: genius co-writing diversity vs model self-consistency diversity). Rationale: tests the user theory (multiple answers together, genius reasons over them) against the strongest standard baseline (self-consistency) in the same batched pool. No results were reported from the voided interim slice.
